concept.name: Change of character
concept.definition: In SMC/ICT vocabulary, the first structural break against the prevailing trend — e.g., in an uptrend, the first close below a higher low — read as an early signal that order flow may be shifting. It is the counter-trend counterpart of a trend-continuing break of structure; a discretionary convention with no canonical authority.
concept.intuition: The first crack in the trend's rhythm: the market does something it hasn't been doing, hinting the character of the move is changing.
concept.mechanics: After establishing the trend's swing sequence, mark the most recent higher low (uptrend) or lower high (downtrend); a decisive break of that pivot against the trend is the change of character. SMC models typically require a preceding liquidity sweep and subsequent displacement before treating it as tradable evidence.
concept.failure_modes: CHoCH signals proliferate on lower timeframes and most are noise within higher-timeframe trends; deep pullbacks routinely trigger counter-trend structure breaks without reversing the main trend.
concept.misconceptions: That a CHoCH is a sell/buy signal by itself; within SMC it is context requiring confirmation (displacement, a return to an order block or gap), not an entry trigger.
concept.example: After a sweep of the prior high, an uptrending pair closes below its last higher low on the 15-minute chart — a CHoCH that SMC traders take as the first evidence of a possible short-side shift.
